Definition: properly, to miscarry, i.e. suffer abortion; by analogy, to bereave (literally or figuratively)
BiblicalUsage: Shakol is to bereave, to take children away until a mother or a father is left empty. Jacob cried it over his sons, me have ye bereaved of my children, Joseph is not and Simeon is not, and Samuel told Agag that as his sword had made women childless so his own mother would be childless. God turns the word into judgment, promising to bereave a people of their children and send famine and evil beasts that shall bereave the land.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe bereavement is the sharpest of God's judgments, because it strikes the home first. The God who can bereave can also restore, and Jacob's cry was answered when Joseph stood alive before him.
